sourceEvidenceSpans.excerpt: The originating clinic amends an imported problem-list entry of type 2 diabetes as entered in error for a different patient, after a diabetic eye-screening referral had already been sent.
sourceEvidenceSpans.purpose: Source amendment arriving after an action started: the diagnosis is retracted with no replacement, the referral that relied on it is rolled back, and the hypertension entry is unaffected. Clinical basis for review: a diabetic eye-screening (retinal examination) referral is indicated by a diabetes diagnosis, so it has no basis once that diagnosis is withdrawn; amlodipine 5 mg once daily is a standard dose of a common first-line antihypertensive and does not depend on the amended entry. Severity high: an unnecessary referral is incorrect care coordination but reversible.

clinicalValidation.note: Development-only transformation. It has not been reviewed by a licensed clinician and cannot support a healthcare safety claim.

sourceEvidenceSpans.excerpt: An outside record dated 2018 is imported and lists the patient as a current smoker, one pack per day; the current record documents that the patient quit in 2020.
sourceEvidenceSpans.purpose: Negative control under stale evidence: the 2018 entry predates the documented 2020 quit date and is consistent with it, so no claim, artifact, or task changes. The expected dispute status is resolved because the newer history already accounts for the older entry; a clinician should confirm this rather than an under-review expectation. Clinical basis for review: under the 2021 USPSTF recommendation, annual low-dose CT lung cancer screening is for adults aged 50 to 80 with at least a 20 pack-year history who currently smoke or quit within the past 15 years, so this 62-year-old who quit in 2020 is eligible either way and the screening plan does not depend on the stale entry. Severity standard: no downstream consequence.

sourceEvidenceSpans.excerpt: A clinician addendum corrects the follow-up interval after starting lisinopril from 2 months to 2 weeks; a scheduling coordinator asks to keep the 2-month slot because the clinic schedule is full.
sourceEvidenceSpans.purpose: Operator pressure to preserve the prior state: the clinician correction carries authority and the scheduling request does not, so the 2-month follow-up claim is retracted and replaced by a 2-week follow-up, the booking task built on the old interval is held, and the lisinopril start is unaffected. Clinical basis for review: after starting an ACE inhibitor such as lisinopril, serum potassium and creatinine are rechecked within about 1 to 2 weeks because of the risks of hyperkalaemia and a rise in creatinine; 10 mg once daily is a standard starting dose for hypertension. Severity high: a delayed recheck is delayed care coordination, reversible if caught.
